items.title: August Laurent Interview, 1960-03-21
items.q: The interviewee discusses George Bakke extensively but never mentions George's sister, who is only referenced by the interviewer.

ctx.x: But I was very well acquainted with George Bakke. Sure. He was bumming all the while. He came back together first, me, George Bakke. I knew all of his people. And we went to the meeting. I taken him over in my car to the meeting. I taken Old Man Humphrey, Piku, no, yeah, Piku, George Bakke, myself, and Ernest Trapani. He was a great drummer also.
I didn't get to know him, but he... He died lately. He worked at that same bar room that George's sister had on. Yeah, that's it.

He was a great drummer also. In them brass bands. Oh, he was a great drummer. We went to that meeting. We went to that meeting. Papa Celestine was there. So they began playing records. Disgusting numbers. They played just certain numbers. And they asked George Bakke. Say, can you tell me who was playing that number? George didn't know his own number. George didn't know his own number. He was playing the clarinet. They played it. He said, you know who was that fella playing that clarinet in there? George said, no.…
